articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document is the "SJAA EPHEMERIS," the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association, specifically Volume 5, Number 7, published in July 1994. It serves as a periodical or newsletter for the association members, likely containing astronomical information relevant to that month.

articles.title: The Eyepiece
articles.summary: The article recounts the author's experience at the RTMC conference, detailing impressive amateur telescopes like a 41-inch Dobsonian and a 6-inch offering superior Jupiter views, alongside commercial vendor displays and a remembrance of Cliff Holmes. It also provides a comprehensive schedule of upcoming astronomical events for July and August, including star parties, general meetings, classes, and a public star party, highlighting the Shoemaker-Levy impact on Jupiter and a talk on the Perseid meteor shower.

articles.title: Pigs
articles.summary: A group of observers attended the Halls Valley star party at Grant Ranch County Park on Saturday, May 14th. While the sky was clear at sundown, cloud cover became solid by 11:30 PM, limiting observing opportunities. A unique aspect of the evening was the presence of a family of wild pigs nearby, making it an interesting, if not ideal, night away from the city.

articles.title: The Elusive Annular Eclipse of 10 May 1994
articles.summary: Ernie Piini recounts his challenging attempt to observe the 10 May 1994 Annular Eclipse in the south-central USA with his brother, despite meticulous planning and custom equipment. They faced severe weather, including a tornado alert and heavy rain, which ultimately prevented them from seeing the annularity, though they did capture some partial phases. The article also details his technical preparations, extensive travel, and post-eclipse sightseeing, including a visit to Kitt Peak Observatory.

articles.title: RTMC 1994 REFLECTIONS OF A NOVICE
articles.summary: A novice amateur astronomer, Bob Elsberry, recounts his first experience at the 1994 Riverside Telescope Makers Conference (RTMC), initially approaching it with a mix of excitement, awe, and fear. He describes overcoming his apprehensions, enjoying the well-organized event, partaking in the 'buying frenzy' for astronomy bargains, and being inspired by the diverse and impressive homemade telescopes. Elsberry concludes with a newfound enthusiasm for the RTMC, eager to return with his own custom-built telescope.

articles.title: Treasurer's report
articles.summary: This document presents a concise financial report from Treasurer Jim Hodgers, detailing various fund balances as of May 14th or after the April issue. It lists balances for the checkbook, Observatory Fund, Gregory Fund, and Ephemeris pool, noting that the checkbook balance includes auction proceeds.

articles.title: Viewing The Southern Skies From The Big Island Of Hawaii
articles.summary: The article recounts a trip to the Big Island of Hawaii, specifically Kona, for observing the southern skies. While the island offered advantages like closer proximity to southern celestial objects and island-wide low-pressure sodium streetlights, the author faced challenges with consistent evening cloud cover. Despite this, they managed to observe Crux, Centaurus, and Omega Centauri from Kona, and planned a stargazing tour to Mauna Kea for improved viewing conditions.

articles.title: Hawaii
articles.summary: The author recounts a trip to Mauna Kea, Hawaii, detailing the journey to the summit, observations of telescopes, and a sunset viewing. They then attended a star party at 9000ft, where they observed Venus, Jupiter, and various deep-sky objects, including the easily visible Milky Way, Eta Carinae nebula, and the spectacular open star cluster NGC-3532, despite some issues with seeing conditions.

articles.title: Credits!
articles.summary: An editor issued a correction regarding a previous article on collimation by Craig Wolford. The editor clarified that Wolford's article originally appeared in the Western Observatorium's publication and thanked Paul Livio for bringing the omission to their attention.

articles.title: Lassen Volcanic National Park Dark Sky Trip
articles.summary: A dark sky observing trip is being organized for Lassen Volcanic National Park from August 5-8, coinciding with a new moon. Attendees have two camping options, Lost Creek (group, tent-only, reservable) and Crags (first-come, no restrictions), with the primary observing site at the Devastated Area. The park is noted for its very dark skies, geothermal features, and family-friendly daytime activities like hiking and fishing.

articles.title: Couple of Things
articles.summary: The article highlights the crucial role of Paul Barton, the telescope loan coordinator, in managing the club's telescope loan program and maintaining the equipment. It urges members to return borrowed telescopes on time or communicate delays to Paul, emphasizing the importance of respecting the loan agreement to ensure the continued availability and quality of this valuable club service for everyone.

articles.title: By Don Machholz
articles.summary: This article provides updates on several comets: Comet Muller (1993p) has dimmed, and Periodic Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 is anticipated to collide with Jupiter in July. It also reports the recovery of Periodic Comet Brooks 2 (1994f) and the discovery of Periodic Comet Shoemaker 4 (1994k), detailing their current and projected brightness, along with orbital periods.

articles.title: EPHEMERIDES
articles.summary: This document provides detailed ephemerides for six comets, including Comet Takamizawa-Levy, Periodic Comet Tempel 1, Periodic Comet Borrelly, Periodic Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9, Comet McNaught-Russell, and Comet Takamizawa, listing their coordinates, elongation, sky visibility, and magnitude from June to August. It highlights the impending collision of Shoemaker-Levy 9 with Jupiter on July 20.64 UT. Additionally, it features a calendar of events for the SJAA (likely an astronomy club), including general meetings, star parties, and astronomy classes, from July to December 1994.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Status
articles.summary: This article outlines the current status of the SJAA telescope loaner program, detailing the availability and usage of various telescopes. It lists who currently possesses each telescope, their due dates, and notes which are available, on hold, or assigned to specific members on a waiting list. Members interested in borrowing a telescope are instructed to contact Paul Barton to be added to a list.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: This document, titled "ASTRO ADS," serves as a free classifieds section for noncommercial advertisers to sell astronomically related products or services. It features listings for various used astronomical equipment, including telescopes (e.g., Astro Physics refractor, Celestron SP-C8, Meade SCT), mounts, eyepieces, and an observatory. Advertisers are instructed to submit their ads by the 12th of each month for a three-month run.

articles.title: July 1994
articles.summary: This document serves as an astronomical almanac for July 1994, detailing lunar phases and the positions, magnitudes, rise, transit, and set times for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, and the Sun. It also provides astronomical twilight and sidereal time information, and highlights the 'Darkest Saturday Night' on July 9th for optimal viewing, with all times specified in Pacific Daylight Time.

articles.title: Offices and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the members of an organization's Board of Directors and key office holders, including their names and contact numbers. It also identifies individuals responsible for ephemeris contributions, editing, and distribution roles within the organization.

articles.title: Collision of periodic Comet S/L-9 with Jupiter
articles.summary: This article discusses the predicted collision of fragments from periodic Comet S/L-9 with Jupiter throughout July 1994. The comet had fragmented into a 'string of pearls' after a close encounter with Jupiter in 1992, making this the first predicted and observed comet-planet collision. The author provides observational details, including impact locations on Jupiter's southern hemisphere and a detailed table of predicted collision times for various fragments (A through W).

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association publishes "EPHEMERIS" monthly, encouraging members to submit articles. Submissions, preferably in text file format on a 3-1/2" diskette, must be typed and sent to editor Bob Madden by the 12th of the preceding month for publication.

articles.title: Membership only: $12   Membership / S&T: $32   Junior (under 18): $20
articles.summary: This document is a membership application form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). It outlines different membership tiers—Membership Only ($12), Membership/S&T ($32), and Junior (under 18) ($20)—along with instructions for submission via mail or in person, and contact information for their treasurer.
